name: D1-backed append-only food-draft repository and migration definition
phase: Specification only; implementation requires separate explicit authorization
objective: Define an injected D1 adapter preserving FOOD-001B exactly, plus an unapplied migration definition and real local SQL integration verification, without runtime activation or sale authority.
databasePlacement: Use injected narrow D1 database access only; define the food-local database/result interface within the adapter.
Architecturally target a future dedicated RIVER_FOOD_DB. Do not create, provision, configure or bind it in this slice.
Do not reuse commerce, CRM, insurance, Sesh or identity databases merely because they exist.
Ownership and authorization remain outside the repository. Identity possession grants no access authority; no principals, sessions or permission integration.

columns: identity_order_key TEXT NOT NULL COLLATE BINARY
identity_order_key TEXT NOT NULL COLLATE BINARY
food_product_draft_snapshots.foreignKey: (recipe_id, recipe_version) REFERENCES food_recipe_draft_snapshots(recipe_id, version), with no cascade deletion

constraintsAndIndexes: Composite primary-key identity comparisons are binary, case-sensitive and exact; all primary-key columns explicitly NOT NULL.
CHECK typeof(version) = 'integer' AND version BETWEEN 1 AND 9007199254740991 on both tables; apply the same bounds to product recipe_version.
Require serialization_format_version to be the supported integer format version 1; application decoding independently rejects unsupported formats.
Index each table by identity_order_key COLLATE BINARY, canonical identity and version for deterministic latest listing; composite primary keys support exact reads and ascending history.
Index product recipe_id/recipe_version for reference lookup; verify query plans before adding further indexes.
Evidence remains inside the canonical subject-bound snapshot. No timestamps, ownership fields, completeness projections, approval fields or sale-readiness fields.

immutableHistory: Migration-defined BEFORE UPDATE and BEFORE DELETE triggers reject mutation on both tables using RAISE(ABORT). No cascade deletion, replace, upsert-update, overwrite, renumbering, merging or evidence retargeting.
Applied migration history is immutable. Later corrections require forward migrations; include no destructive rollback SQL.
Migration definition belongs in this slice; database provisioning, configuration and execution against configured databases remain deferred.

unicodeOrdering.algorithm: For each canonical JavaScript identity string, iterate indexes 0 through length - 1 using charCodeAt (UTF-16 code units, not code points). Encode each unit as exactly four lowercase hexadecimal digits, then concatenate.
requirements: The ordering key is derived metadata and never replaces the canonical identity or participates in domain snapshot equality.
Persist the same derived key for every version of an identity. Recompute and verify it on every returned row; mismatch fails closed.

Latest listing and afterId keyset predicates use the derived key with COLLATE BINARY, with canonical identity as a defensive deterministic tie-breaker. Convert the validated canonical afterId internally; expose only FOOD-001B identity cursors.
History is scoped to an exact identity and ordered by version ascending; its identity ordering key is constant and verified. Never reorder history by insertion order.
Test BMP, surrogate-pair supplementary characters, ASCII/non-ASCII mixtures, prefixes and case distinctions, including identities where SQLite text order diverges from JavaScript UTF-16 order.

sqlInvariants: Enforce composite uniqueness, positive safe-integer version bounds, exact product-to-recipe composite foreign key and immutable history in SQL.
For a new initial insert, require version 1 and absence of any stored history for that identity inside the conditional INSERT statement.

For a new revision insert, check exact predecessor existence, next version = expectedPreviousVersion + 1 and maximum stored version = expectedPreviousVersion inside the conditional INSERT statement. Prior application reads alone do not establish concurrency safety.
Use targeted ON CONFLICT(identity, version) DO NOTHING, never broad INSERT OR IGNORE that could conceal other constraint failures.

A unique key alone does not prove initial/consecutive/latest-version rules, retry equality or valid domain history. Conditional-write invariants govern adapter writes; do not claim every arbitrary direct SQL insert is domain validated.
applicationInvariants: Implement the existing FoodDraftRepository contract and reuse FOOD-001A validators/revision constructors and FOOD-001B canonical serialization/deserialization unchanged.

Validate canonical branded IDs, exact operation shape, expected predecessor, positive safe versions and overflow before retry interpretation. Initial versions must be 1; revisions exactly predecessor + 1.

Load and validate the exact immutable predecessor; for products validate both old and new exact recipe references using stored snapshots. Missing referenced recipe is a validation failure; missing predecessor/version conflict returns conflict as in FOOD-001B.

Preserve array order, fixed canonical object ordering, format version, evidence subject/version bindings, unknown/pending/undisclosed/unfavorable/inconclusive findings and historical label references.

Validate limits/cursors without coercion and verify ordering keys and all row/envelope/domain metadata, including recipe columns. Reject corrupt JSON, unsupported formats, stale evidence, missing references and noncanonical stored payloads rather than repairing them.

Return newly detached, recursively frozen snapshots and frozen result/page containers. No completeness or approval state is persisted or projected; requiredEvidencePresent remains independent of unresolvedReviews.

appendConcurrency.atomicOperation: Use one transactional D1 batch containing the conditional insert followed by the exact-key read needed to determine the outcome; validate batch result count, success and insert meta.changes.
interpretation: Insert changes 1 plus a valid exact matching canonical stored payload means created.
Insert changes 0 plus a valid exact identical canonical stored payload means already-present.
Insert changes 0 plus a valid differing canonical stored payload means conflict.
Insert changes 0 plus no exact row means conflict.
Missing/unexpected metadata, malformed row, format/serialization mismatch, corrupt stored state, or changes 1 without the exact matching row means storage failure.
requirements: Compare complete FOOD-001B canonical serialized envelopes byte-for-byte, not parsed partial fields, hashes alone, timestamps or derived projections.

Historical identical retries remain permissible after later versions exist, provided operation shape, exact predecessor and domain/reference validation pass. The conditional insert may do nothing because predecessor is no longer latest; the existing exact row still determines valid retry equality.

Two independent writers against one predecessor can create only one next identity/version. Others compare exact stored state and return conflict or already-present; never select another version silently.
Zero affected rows are not a SQL error and do not themselves distinguish retry from conflict. Foreign-key/trigger failures and unexpected batch results must not be recast as benign duplicate success.
Transport/batch uncertainty propagates as failure. Callers may retry the same canonical operation; never invent success after uncertain writes.
Use primary-consistent injected access for predecessor/reference reads and outcome interpretation; replica freshness cannot be assumed. No session/auth/runtime wiring is introduced.

Explicitly verify transactional batch visibility and rollback, conditional insertion, ON CONFLICT and affected-row behavior with the local integration harness. Local verification does not prove remote/production D1 behavior.
Exact missing reads return not-found; malformed stored data throws FoodDraftStorageError. Invalid caller values use FoodDraftValidationError; retain FOOD-001B error/outcome distinctions.
Product reads preserve and validate the recorded exact historical recipe ID/version; never substitute latest. Recipes may exist without products.
History uses afterVersion and ascending versions. Latest uses afterId and the maximum stored version per identity ordered by verified UTF-16 key.

Reject invalid limits, unknown options, malformed/wrong-kind cursors without coercion or clamping. Use bounded LIMIT limit + 1 retrieval where needed, never load entire histories to paginate in JavaScript.
Return nextCursor only when more matching results exist, using the last returned version/identity. Empty pages have no cursor; pagination does not promise a cross-call consistent snapshot.

integrationHarnessInspection.method: Inspection of installed metadata/types/code and existing test sources, followed by isolated throwaway Miniflare worker-side SQL probes; no repository changes or configured/local project/remote database access.
integrationHarnessInspection.installedMechanism: Installed Miniflare 5.20260903.0-alpha with workerd 1.20260903.1, using convertV4MiniflareOptions, cf: false, d1Persist: false and a synthetic isolated D1 database identifier.
integrationHarnessInspection.existingTestRunner: node:test with tsx; inspected existing D1 adapter tests use fakes. No existing Miniflare SQL integration test was found in src/tools.
integrationHarnessInspection.recommendation: Define an inline test worker with the FOOD_TEST D1 binding and exercise D1 inside that worker. Bridge the repository's injected narrow D1 interface through dispatchFetch(), preserving each repository batch as one worker-side env.FOOD_TEST.batch() call.
accessRequirements: Do not use Miniflare's Node-side getD1Database() proxy for FOOD-001C integration tests: it stalls in the current installed alpha environment.
Multiple bridge/repository instances in a test must share the same isolated Miniflare database to exercise competing writers.
Execute the actual FOOD-001C migration SQL only inside this isolated harness and dispose Miniflare after tests.
Use no Wrangler config, project binding, configured/local project database or remote database.
verifiedLocalCapabilities: SQL execution through the inline worker-side D1 binding.
Trigger rejection, observed with an UPDATE rejection trigger.
Per-statement meta.changes, including insert changes 1 and conflict suppression changes 0.
Insert-to-read visibility inside one D1 batch.
Failed-batch rollback, with the earlier insert absent after a later trigger failure.
remainingRequiredVerification: The actual FOOD-001C tests must still verify both UPDATE and DELETE immutability triggers, revision concurrency, exact append outcomes, bounded listings, Unicode ordering, exact historical recipe references and malformed/corrupt row handling.
Observed generic harness capabilities do not replace any FOOD-001C unit or integration requirement.
integrationHarnessInspection.assessment: The worker-side access method is locally verified and uses installed tooling without adding a dependency or testing framework. Local Miniflare/workerd verification does not prove remote production behavior, replication consistency or production transport-failure behavior.
integrationHarnessInspection.stopCondition: Before implementation recheck installed harness availability. If it cannot meaningfully verify actual database semantics, record the blocker and STOP before implementation; do not introduce a new framework without separate approval or claim fake tests prove concurrency.

tests: Unit tests cover FOOD-001B contract parity, canonical retry equality, malformed inputs, errors, corruption, metadata disagreement, stale evidence, detached/frozen results and source isolation.

Actual local SQLite/D1-compatible integration tests exercise migration constraints and UPDATE/DELETE triggers, version bounds, composite foreign keys, conditional initial/revision inserts, targeted ON CONFLICT and affected-row metadata.
Verify transaction/batch insert-to-read visibility and full rollback on a later failing statement; validate missing/unexpected result metadata fails closed.

Use two independent repository instances on the same isolated local database for competing initial/revision appends: exactly one creation, appropriate identical/conflicting retries, no overwrite or renumbering.
Verify missing/skipped/stale predecessors, overflow, historical identical retries after later versions, and exact historical recipe references after newer recipes exist.
Verify canonical round trips and corruption failures, format/row/envelope/order-key/reference disagreement, unresolved/adverse findings and absence of persisted completeness or sale authority.
Verify Unicode ordering against FOOD-001B JavaScript ordering, deterministic latest selection/history, bounded limit + 1 SQL retrieval, 20/100 limits and implementation-neutral cursors.
Keep local harness evidence distinct from later remote/production verification; no production concurrency claim and no configured-database migration execution.
provenance: FOOD-001A and FOOD-001B specifications and unchanged modules are semantic authorities.
https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/reference/migrations/ documents numbered migration definitions and tracking; these references do not establish tested runtime behavior.
deferredScope: No binding/config changes, database creation/provisioning, migration execution against any configured database, runtime wiring, River OS UI, routes or auth integration.
No commerce registration, checkout, Stripe/payment, fulfillment, accounting, public counters, community activation, deployment or production data.
No insurance, Sesh, creator or unrelated subsystem changes; preserve additive directions and external legal/tax/safety/water/payment/community readiness gates.
currentTaskBoundary: Create only this specification. Do not implement, create migrations, execute/access D1, change configuration, stage, commit or push.
nextStep: Review this specification and separately authorize implementation only if the existing local harness can meaningfully verify the required database semantics.
